metadata.label: Run Permits Actor
metadata.note: HTTP v4 'Make a request'. Calls the permits actor synchronously; the dataset items array comes back as this module's 'data' output. Paste your Apify API token into the Authorization header (keep the 'Bearer ' prefix). In the published template this header Value is a wizard field with help text.

metadata.label: Iterate dataset items
metadata.note: Built-in Flow Control > Iterator. Fires once per array item so the downstream HTTP call runs per item instead of once for the whole batch. Ships with every Make plan; no connection needed.

mapper.jsonStringBodyContent: {  "channel": "REPLACE_WITH_SLACK_CHANNEL_ID",  "text": "New permit with a contractor lead: {{2.contractor_name}} - {{2.contractor_phone}} | Permit {{2.permit_number}} ({{2.permit_type}}), issued {{2.issued_date}} | {{2.address}}, {{2.zip}} | {{2.work_description}} | valuation {{2.valuation}} | {{2.source_url}}"}

metadata.label: Post Contractor to Slack (per item)
metadata.note: HTTP v4 'Make a request'. Calls Slack's Web API (chat.postMessage) directly, so no Slack app connection is needed - only a bot token with chat:write in the Authorization header (wizard field with help text in the published template). Set 'channel' to your Slack channel ID. Add a Filter between module 2 and this one (contractor_phone is not empty) so only permits with a dialable number post.

notes: HTTP modules are the current v4 app: module id 'http:MakeRequest', version 4 (the old v3 'HTTP (legacy)' module id was 'http:ActionSendData').
Schedule is not encoded in the blueprint. After import, click the clock icon on the scenario and set it to run daily.
Replace every YOUR-*-TOKEN and REPLACE_WITH_* placeholder before running.
In the published Make template the Authorization header Value on each module is marked 'Use in Wizard' + 'Use as default value' and carries help text pointing at the token page.
